523.synopsis:
Opens the file named at HL for output: sets the mode to OP_OUT and continues in OpenRead's
common part (skip leading spaces, open with GN_Opf).
Entry: HL = filename (local pointer).
Exit: IX = file handle; Fc = 0.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code (from GN_Opf).
Changes: AF, DE, HL, IX.
Keeps: BC.

527.synopsis:
Opens the file named at HL for input. Skips leading spaces, then calls GN_Opf with B = 0
(local name), DE = 3 so no explicit name is kept, and C = $FF. OpenWrite enters the same
code with OP_OUT.
Entry: HL = filename (local pointer).
Exit: IX = file handle; Fc = 0; HL = first non-space of the name.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code (from GN_Opf).
Changes: AF, DE, HL, IX.
Keeps: BC.

551.synopsis:
CLI script ".T>:PRT", CR, ".S", 0: tees the CLI's output to the printer, then ends its
input. DC_Alt starts it with DC_Icl ([]+P) when no CLI is running.

562.synopsis:
CLI script ".T<:RAM.-/K.sgn", CR, ".S", 0: tees keyboard input into the file K.sgn, then
ends its input. DC_Alt starts it with DC_Icl ([]+K) when no CLI is running.

565.synopsis:
Entry inside RedirInKsgn_cli: the filename ":RAM.-/K.sgn", ended by CR. DC_Alt opens it with
OpenWrite to rebind a running CLI's input tee ([]+K).

581.synopsis:
CLI script ".T>:RAM.-/S.sgn", CR, ".S", 0: tees the screen output into the file S.sgn, then
ends its input. DC_Alt starts it with DC_Icl ([]+S) when no CLI is running.

584.synopsis:
Entry inside RedirOutSsgn_cli: the filename ":RAM.-/S.sgn", ended by CR. DC_Alt opens it
with OpenWrite to rebind a running CLI's output tee ([]+S).

889.synopsis:
Forgets the application waiting to be run: clears pIdxRunProcIX and the bank byte of
eIdxRunProc.
Entry: none.
Exit: A = 0.
Changes: AF.

1291.synopsis:
A single zero byte, an empty string. DC_Dq for the default directory returns BHL =
DC_BNK:zero_byte when the Filer process has no associated directory.

1952.synopsis:
Reads the 3-byte link at IY into CDE.
Entry: IY = list node (link at +0..+2: low, high, bank).
Exit: C = bank; DE = address.
Changes: C, DE.

1962.synopsis:
Reads the 3-byte link at IY into BHL.
Entry: IY = list node or list head (link at +0..+2: low, high, bank).
Exit: B = bank; HL = address.
Changes: B, HL.

1972.synopsis:
Fills B bytes from HL with zero.
Entry: HL = start; B = count (0 means 256).
Exit: HL = byte after the block; B = 0; A = 0.
Changes: AF, B, HL.

1978.synopsis:
Returns an error to the caller of a DC call: stores A in the OS frame's A and sets Fc in its
F.
Entry: IY = OS frame; A = error code.
Exit: frame A = error code; frame Fc = 1.
Changes: none.

1986.synopsis:
Loads the caller's HL from the OS frame.
Entry: IY = OS frame.
Exit: HL = caller's HL.
Changes: HL.

1993.synopsis:
Reads a process block's stacked environment, dynamic ID and handle; falls into
GetProcHandle.
Entry: IY = process block (bound).
Exit: BHL = prc_stkProcEnv; C = prc_dynid; DE = prc_hndl.
Changes: BC, DE, HL.

2005.synopsis:
Reads a process block's application handle.
Entry: IY = process block (bound).
Exit: DE = prc_hndl.
Changes: DE.

2012.synopsis:
Stores IX as a process block's application handle.
Entry: IY = process block (bound); IX = handle.
Exit: prc_hndl = IX; DE = IX.
Changes: DE.

2200.synopsis:
Tests whether IX is the :INP handle (phnd_Ihn).
Entry: IX = handle.
Exit: Fz = 1 when IX = phnd_Ihn; HL = IX - phnd_Ihn.
Changes: F, BC, HL.

2300.synopsis:
Rebinds one stream of a CLI with RebindStream, then frees the CLI with FreeCli when none of
its six streams is left open.
Entry: IY = CLI block (bound in S1); BC = offset of the stream word (cli_instream ...); A =
its CLIS_xxx flag; IX = new handle (0 closes the stream).
Exit: as RebindStream, or as FreeCli when the CLI was freed.

2792.synopsis:
Loads the timeout stored in the CLI block (the BC that DC_In was given).
Entry: IY = CLI block (bound).
Exit: BC = cli_argB:cli_argC.
Changes: BC.

2799.synopsis:
Frees every CLI: calls FreeCli until it reports that no CLI is left.
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc = 0; A = RC_Eof (from the last FreeCli); no CLI remains.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX, IY.

2950.synopsis:
Points HL at the CLI's prefix sequence buffer, used with OS_Isq and OS_Wsq.
Entry: IY = CLI block (bound).
Exit: HL = IY + cli_PrefixBuffer.
Changes: BC, HL.

3119.synopsis:
Writes a byte to a stream with OS_Pbt, using the CLI's stored timeout.
Entry: A = byte; IX = handle; IY = CLI block (bound).
Exit: Fc = 0.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code (from OS_Pbt).
Keeps: BC.

3127.synopsis:
Frees the most recently invoked CLI, the head of eIdxCliList.
1. Binds the CLI block into S1 and closes its six streams (RebindStream with IX = 0).
2. Unlinks it from the list and releases the block with OS_Mfr (pIdxMemHandle).
3. Decrements the CLI use count (OS_Cli, CL_DEC).
Entry: none.
Exit: Fc and A as OS_Cli returns them; the CLI's bank stays bound in S1.
Error: Fc = 1, A = RC_Eof when no CLI is running.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX, IY (IY = eIdxCliList).

3224.synopsis:
Writes CDE as the 3-byte link at IY.
Entry: IY = list node or list head; C = bank; DE = address.
Exit: (IY+0..2) = E, D, C.
Changes: none.

3503.synopsis:
Reads CLI input up to and including the next CR, then clears CLIF_B_NOTBOL (at the start of
a line again).
Entry: IY = CLI block (bound).
Exit: Fc = 0; A = CR.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code (from ReadCliChar).
Changes: AF, BC, HL.

3516.synopsis:
Reads the rest of the CLI line as a filename and opens it for input (GetRedirectName,
OpenRead).
Entry: IY = CLI block (bound).
Exit: IX = file handle; Fc = 0.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code.

3523.synopsis:
Reads the rest of the CLI line as a filename and opens it for output (GetRedirectName,
OpenWrite).
Entry: IY = CLI block (bound).
Exit: IX = file handle; Fc = 0.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code.

3530.synopsis:
Fills the CLI line buffer up to the end of the line (sets CLIF_B_FILLALL, FillCLIBuffer),
then falls into GetLineBuffer to point HL at it.
Entry: IY = CLI block (bound).
Exit: HL = cli_LineBuffer in the CLI block; Fc = 0.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code (from FillCLIBuffer).
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX.

3538.synopsis:
Points HL at the CLI's line buffer.
Entry: IY = CLI block (bound).
Exit: HL = IY + cli_LineBuffer; Fc = 0.
Changes: F, HL.
Keeps: DE.

3644.synopsis:
Takes the next character of CLI input: tops up the line buffer with FillCLIBuffer, removes
the first byte and moves the rest down.
Entry: IY = CLI block (bound).
Exit: A = C = character; Fc = 0; Fz = 1 when the character is 0.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code (from FillCLIBuffer).
Changes: AF, BC, HL.
Keeps: DE, IX.

3685.synopsis:
Reads the CLI's input stream into the free end of its line buffer with OS_Gbt and the stored
timeout. It reads one byte, or, when CLIF_B_FILLALL is set (it is then cleared), up to a CR
or until the buffer is full. Bytes below $20 other than CR are dropped.
Entry: IY = CLI block (bound).
Exit: Fc = 0 (also when the read failed but the buffer holds bytes).
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code when the read failed and the buffer is empty.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX (IX = input stream).

3764.synopsis:
Reads the head of the CLI list, the most recently invoked CLI.
Entry: none.
Exit: BHL = CLI block; Fz = 1 when no CLI is running; A = B or H or L.
Changes: AF, B, HL.
Keeps: IY.

4081.synopsis:
Filename ":EPR.?/Boot.cli", 0: a Boot.cli in any file area. Index tries it after RamBootCLI
when it is started the first time.

4097.synopsis:
Filename ":RAM.?/Boot.cli", 0: a Boot.cli in any RAM device. Index tries it first when it is
started the first time.

4113.synopsis:
Opens the named file for input (GN_Opf, with a 256-byte explicit name buffer on the stack)
and starts a new CLI that reads it (DC_Icl with BHL = 0, IX = the file). When DC_Icl fails
the file is closed again.
Entry: HL = filename (local pointer).
Exit: Fc = 0 when the CLI was started; when DC_Icl failed, Fc as OS_Cl returns it.
Error: Fc = 1, A = error code when the file cannot be opened.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, IX, AF'.

4233.synopsis:
Index's entry after its first run (and after the boot scripts were tried).
1. When an application is marked to start at boot (pIdxAutoRunAppl), clears the mark and
enters it.
2. Otherwise reads the "NAME" mailbox (OS_Sr, SR_RPD) into App_Buff1; when it holds a name,
goes to AskInstall.
3. Otherwise falls into IndexRedraw.
Entry: none.

4273.synopsis:
Redraws Index and falls into MainLoop. When an application ended with an error (IDXF2_ERROR
in ubIdxFlags2), goes to ShowExitError instead. The commands jump here after changing the
display.
Entry: none.

4284.synopsis:
Index's command loop: reads a key with OS_In (marking IDXF1_B_INSIDEOZ while waiting) and
calls MayInitIndex before and after. On an error, RC_Quit exits Index with OS_Bye, RC_Draw
goes to IndexRedraw, anything else reads again. A key goes to main_2.
Entry: none.

4311.synopsis:
Entry inside MainLoop: dispatches a key. '0'-'3' go to cmd_ramcrd_sel, 'Y'/'N'/'y'/'n' to
cmd_insrmv_sel, other plain keys are ignored. A 0 is followed by a command code; codes 1-15
jump through the table at main_3, others are ignored.
Entry: A = key from OS_In.

4384.synopsis:
Table of 15 words: Index's command handlers for command codes 1-15: right, left, up, down,
enter, escape, kill, card, 0 (the purge command, removed), info, install, remove, nq,
update, hard reset. Code 9 would jump to address 0.

4417.synopsis:
Clears IDXF1_B_INSIDEOZ. When IDXF1_B_INIT is set, clears it and rebuilds Index: resets the
selection (InitIndex), rescans the application keys (InitKeys) and redraws (DrawWindow).
Entry: HL = ubIdxPubFlags.
Keeps: AF.

5318.synopsis:
GN_Win block of the APPLICATIONS window: window 2 with bars, shelf brackets and an 8-pixel
banner; X = 0, Y = 0, width 18, height 8; banner text at appl_banner.

5338.synopsis:
GN_Win block of the SUSPENDED ACTIVITIES window: window 3 with bars, shelf brackets and an
8-pixel banner; X = 20, Y = 0, width 56, height 8; banner text at proc_banner.

5366.synopsis:
Selects and clears the application window and lists up to 6 applications from
ubIdxTopApplication on, leaving out Index, each with its key (PrintApp). Stores the count in
ubIdxNApplDisplayed.
Entry: none.

5425.synopsis:
Selects and clears the process window and lists up to 6 suspended processes from
ubIdxTopProcess on (PrintProcess). When the top process no longer exists, restarts from 0
(and resets ubIdxSelectorPos when the process window is active). Stores the count in
ubIdxNProcDisplayed and prints "NONE" when there is none.
Entry: none.

5563.synopsis:
Draws the selection bar: toggles reverse on, applies it over the selected line
(RemoveHighlight) and toggles reverse off again.
Entry: none.
Changes: AF, BC.

5572.synopsis:
Moves to column 0 of the selected line (ubIdxSelectorPos) and applies the current attributes
over it with ApplyA: 50 characters in the application window, 83 in the process window
(ubIdxActiveWindow). With no attribute on, this removes the bar.
Entry: none.
Changes: AF, BC.

5771.synopsis:
Compares the low byte of an application handle with a key table entry.
Entry: IX = application handle; HL = key table entry.
Exit: Fz = 1 when IXL = (HL); A = IXL.
Changes: AF.

5881.synopsis:
Moves the cursor to column B, row C of the current window (1, "3@", X, Y).
Entry: B = column; C = row.
Changes: AF.

5898.synopsis:
Moves the cursor to column A of the current line (1, "2X", X).
Entry: A = column.
Changes: AF.

5911.synopsis:
Toggles the tiny font (1, "T").
Entry: none.

5931.synopsis:
Moves the cursor to the top left of the current window and clears to the end of the window
(1, "2C", $FE), clearing all of it.
Entry: none.

5944.synopsis:
Selects and initialises window 2, the application window (1, "2I2").
Entry: none.

5952.synopsis:
Selects and initialises window 3, the process window (1, "2I3").
Entry: none.

5960.synopsis:
Scrolls the current window up (1, $FF).
Entry: none.

5966.synopsis:
Applies the toggled display attributes to A characters from the cursor (1, "2A", A).
Entry: A = number of characters.
Keeps: A.

5977.synopsis:
Index command "card" (code 8). Fills CardData, 3 bytes per slot 0-3 (RAM banks, file area
banks, ROM banks): RAM from OS_Nq NQ_Mfp, an application card's size from its header byte at
$3FFC of the top bank (NQ_Slt says BU_ROM), the file area from OS_Epr EP_Req. Then it makes
the card window active (ubIdxActiveWindow = 2) and goes to IndexRedraw.
Entry: none.

6203.synopsis:
GN_Win block of the CARDS window: window 4 with bars, shelf brackets and an 8-pixel banner,
drawn as a pop-up on a grey screen; X = 9, Y = 0, width 46, height 8; banner text at
cards_banner.

6216.synopsis:
Prints the rows of the card window for slots 3 down to 0 (GetCardData, DisplayCard).
Entry: CardData filled by cmd_card.
Exit: D = $FF; IY = slot 0's bytes in CardData.

6232.synopsis:
Prints one slot's row of the card window: moves to column 0, row slot + 1, and prints the
ROM size at column 15, the file area at 25 and the RAM at 35 (PrintCardSize).
Entry: D = slot; IY = the slot's 3 bytes in CardData (RAM, file area, ROM banks).
Keeps: DE.

6266.synopsis:
Prints a size in 16K banks as kilobytes at a column: C * 16 in a 4-character field followed
by 'K' (GN_Pdn to the standard output), or " -" when C = 0.
Entry: A = column; C = size in 16K banks.
Keeps: DE.

6331.synopsis:
Clears the current line and prints "Are you sure ? " with the answer in ubIdxYesNo ("Yes" or
"No"), then moves the cursor back onto the answer and switches the cursor on.
Entry: ubIdxYesNo = 'Y'/'y' for yes, anything else for no.
Changes: AF.

6392.synopsis:
Writes the centred "PRESS ESC TO RESUME" line in tiny font (ESC as its key symbol) with
OS_Pout, then turns centring off again. Used by the info, install, remove and update windows
before they wait for ESC.
Entry: none (writes to the current window).

6537.synopsis:
Shows the FreeRAM details of a RAM card: the size column (DispCardSizeClmn), a cleared and
redrawn page map (DispFreeRamMap), the card size and then jumps to the free space text
(bytes and percentage).
Entry: slotno, cardsize and freespace set by GetFreeSpace.

6551.synopsis:
Shows FreeRAM for a slot without a RAM card: clears window 2 and the page map, then selects
and clears window 3 and writes "(None)" there.
Entry: A = error code from GetFreeSpace.
Keeps: AF.

6578.synopsis:
Writes the card size as "(<n>K)" in window 3, where n = cardsize * 16.
Entry: cardsize = size of the card in 16K banks.

6729.synopsis:
Asks OS_Nq NQ_Mfp for the RAM in the slot held in slotno and stores the card size in banks
in cardsize and the free space in bytes (free pages * 256) in freespace.
Entry: slotno = slot number (0-3).
Exit: Fc = 0; cardsize, freespace (32-bit, low word first) set.
Error: Fc = 1, A = RC_Onf when the slot holds no RAM device.
Changes: AF, BC, DE.

6757.synopsis:
Draws the FreeRAM page map: one pixel for each used 256-byte page of the RAM card, each 16K
bank being an 8x8 pixel character block, eight blocks to a row (128K).
1. Binds the card's bottom bank, which holds the allocation table (slot 0: $21), into
segment 1, and the HIRES0 map area (GetMapAddress) into segment 2.
2. For a card below 8 banks it computes a pixel factor by rotating 8 right once per bank
above one; otherwise one pixel per page.
3. Reads the table from $4100 (2 bytes per page, non-zero = used) and plots each used page
(plot_usedpage) while moving the pixel position (update_pixelptr) per pixel.
4. Restores the segment 2 and segment 1 bindings.
Entry: slotno, cardsize.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, AF', BC', DE', HL'.

6851.synopsis:
Plots one pixel of the page map: ORs the column bit D' into the byte at HL' + BC' (the
current row of the current 8x8 block). Works in the alternate set.
Entry: HL' = block base; BC' = row (0-7); D' = column bit; map bound in segment 2.
Changes: none (AF and HL' are kept).

6862.synopsis:
Moves the page map's pixel position one row down in the current 8x8 block; after the eighth
row it calls new_column. Works in the alternate set.
Entry: HL', BC', D', E' = the map position (see DispFreeRamMap).
Changes: F, C', D', E', HL'.

6871.synopsis:
Moves the page map's pixel position to the next pixel column (column bit rotated right);
when the bit leaves the block it calls next_matrix. Then starts again at row 0. Runs with
the alternate set swapped in by update_pixelptr.
Entry: C = 8; D = column bit; HL = block base; E = blocks left in the row.
Exit: C = 0; D = next column bit.

6879.synopsis:
Moves the page map's position to the next 8x8 block: HL += BC (8 bytes on); counts the
blocks of the row in E and reloads it with 8 when a row of eight blocks is done. Runs with
the alternate set swapped in.
Entry: HL = block base; BC = 8; E = blocks left in the row.
Exit: HL = next block; E = blocks left (8 after a full row).

6885.synopsis:
Clears window 2 and writes the size labels beside the page map, right justified: one line
per 128K row with the running card size in K ("128K", "256K", ...), or the card size alone
for a card below 128K.
Entry: cardsize = size of the card in 16K banks.

6940.synopsis:
Inline OS_Pout text inside DispCardSizeClmn: "K ", CR, LF, null, written after each size
label; the code continues after it with the jump back to the label loop.

7010.synopsis:
Selects and clears window 2 with OS_Pout (1,"2C2"). Shared by FreeRAM and the Index's ESC
handling.
Entry: none.

7025.synopsis: The FreeRAM window's banner text: "FREE RAM", null-terminated, named by FreeRamWindowDef.

7034.synopsis:
Index command <>INFO (entry in the command table): shows the SYSTEM INFORMATION window.
1. Gets the :OUT handle (NQ_Ohn) for the number output, opens the window (InfoWdBlock) and
writes the captions OZ, BUILD, MACHINE, TYPE, FREE MEMORY, BATTERY, FREE HANDLES.
2. OZ version and slot (disp_ver); "Z88"; type "expanded" or "unexpanded" from OS_Frm
FA_EOF; battery "good" or "low" from NQ_Btl.
3. Revision (disp_rev) and the build's date and time, assembled in as constants, through
GN_Dei, GN_Pdt and GN_Ptm.
4. Free memory in K (OS_Frm FA_EXT divided by 1024) and free handles (OS_Frm FA_PTR).
5. Sets the active window to 3 (info window, closed by ESC) and jumps to MainLoop.
Entry: none. Does not return: jumps to MainLoop (IX is kept).

7545.synopsis:
GN_Win definition block of the info windows (SYSTEM INFORMATION and the <>NQ windows):
window 2 with bars, shelf brackets and an 8-pixel banner on a greyed screen, at X = 9, Y =
0, 64 wide and 8 high; banner pointer 0, so the banner comes in DE.

7552.synopsis: Banner text of the info window: "SYSTEM INFORMATION", null-terminated.

7571.synopsis:
Writes "rev. " and the OZ revision as 8 hex digits: OS_Nq NQ_Roz returns it in DEBC, written
D, E, B, C with OS_Hout.
Entry: none.

7597.synopsis:
Writes the OZ version as "<major>.<minor>" from the low byte of OS_Frm FA_PTR (high nibble
major, low nibble minor), then " in slot 1" when OS_Ploz says OZ is not running from slot 0.
Entry: none.

7643.synopsis:
The text "unexpanded", null-terminated. cmd_info writes it for an unexpanded Z88 and writes
from 2 bytes on ("expanded") for an expanded one.

7654.synopsis: The text "good", null-terminated: cmd_info's battery state.

7659.synopsis: The text "low", null-terminated: cmd_info's battery state when NQ_Btl reports low.

7663.synopsis:
Index command <>INS (entry in the command table): opens the INSTALL APPLICATION window and
asks for the .APP filename with GN_Sip into App_Buff1 (up to 128 characters). On ENTER it
goes to AskInstall; otherwise it sets the active window to 0 and redraws the Index
(IndexRedraw).
Entry: none. Does not return.

7709.synopsis:
Sets the active window to 4 (install), redraws the install window and shows "Install
<filename>", then asks "Are you sure ?" with Yes as the default (AreYousure) and jumps to
MainLoop; ENTER there runs DoInstall.
Entry: App_Buff1 = filename. Does not return.

7751.synopsis:
Opens the INSTALL APPLICATION window (GN_Win with InstallWdBlock) and defines window 2 as
its text area (58 x 6 at column 13, row 2), selected and cleared.
Entry: none.

7775.synopsis:
GN_Win definition block of the install window: window 2 with bars, shelf brackets and an
8-pixel banner on a greyed screen, at X = 9, Y = 0, 64 wide and 8 high; banner
InstallBanner.

7782.synopsis: Banner text of the install window: "INSTALL APPLICATION", null-terminated.

7802.synopsis:
Installs an application from RAM files: the .APP header and the .AP0 to .AP6 bank files
named by App_Buff1. Run by ENTER after AskInstall.
1. Unless the answer was 'y', sets window 0 and redraws the Index. Otherwise draws the
install window and saves SP in App_Stack for the error exit.
2. Copies 40 bytes of the .APP file to App_Tag (ci_copyfile) and checks the tag (APF_TAG),
at most 8 banks and no patches; RC_Ftm otherwise.
3. Opens a memory handle (OS_Mop) and allocates an installation handle (OS_Fn FN_AH,
HND_INST) that keeps the memory handle.
4. For each bank entry: works out the pages needed, finds a bank (OS_Fma, even when its
App_Even bit is set), allocates the area (OS_Axm) and loads the .AP<n> file into it
(ci_copyfile); bank, offset page and length go to the Fma table (Fma_AP0, 4 bytes each).
5. Takes the application DOR (App_DOR, or the son pointer at $3FC6 of relative bank 63 when
it is 0), stores it in the installation handle and chains it after the last DOR under the
:APP.- front DOR ($4060 in bank $21).
6. Walks the new DOR chain and translates each DOR's bank numbers (segments, topics,
commands, help, tokens, brother) with ci_TranslateBank, counting the applications.
7. Restores SP, polls the keys again (InitKeys), writes "Installation completed." and waits
for ESC (PressEsc), then jumps to MainLoop.
Error: frees the installation handle, memory and file, stores the error code in
ubIdxErrorCode, sets IDXF2_B_ERROR and redraws the Index. Does not return.

8382.synopsis:
Frees the installation handle: clears App_InstHnd and calls OS_Fn FN_FH with B = HND_INST.
Entry: IX = installation handle.

8395.synopsis:
Closes the install's (or update's) memory handle: clears App_MemHnd and calls OS_Mcl, which
frees the memory allocated through it.
Entry: IX = memory handle.

8404.synopsis:
Closes the install's open file: clears App_FileHnd and calls GN_Cl.
Entry: IX = file handle.
Exit: IX = 0.
Changes: AF, HL, IX.

8414.synopsis:
Tests IX for a null handle.
Entry: IX = handle.
Exit: Fz = 1 when IX = 0, Fz = 0 otherwise.
Changes: AF.

8422.synopsis:
Loads one file of the application being installed into memory: puts the extension character
in A into the third place of App_Buff1's 3-letter extension (which must start with 'A'),
opens the file (GN_Opf), binds bank B into segment 1, reads DE bytes to the offset HL
(OS_Mv) and closes the file.
Entry: A = 'P' or '0'-'7'; B = bank; HL = offset in the bank; DE = length; App_Buff1 =
filename.
Exit: file copied; bank B left bound in segment 1; App_FileHnd = 0.
Error: does not return; jumps to the install's error exit (RC_Ftm for a bad extension).
Changes: AF, DE, HL.
Keeps: BC, IX.

8522.synopsis:
Translates a bank number of an application's DOR from its relative form ($F8-$FF for bank 7
to bank 0 of the application) to the bank allocated for it, read from the first byte of its
4-byte entry in the Fma table (Fma_AP0). Bank 0 is left as it is.
Entry: A = relative bank number.
Exit: A = absolute bank number.
Changes: AF.
Keeps: BC, HL.

8544.synopsis:
Index command <>REM (entry in the command table): starts removing the selected application.
Gets its static handle (GetAppByNum) and keeps it in App_RmvHnd; an application that is not
installed (handle below $80) gives RC_Fail, one that runs (DC_Pol with A = $80) gives
RC_Use, both shown through the Index's error flag (IDXF2_B_ERROR) and a redraw. Otherwise
sets the active window to 5, shows "Remove <name>" and asks "Are you sure ?" with No as the
default, then jumps to MainLoop; ENTER there runs DoRemove.
Entry: ubIdxTopApplication + ubIdxSelectorPos = the selected application. Does not return.

8636.synopsis:
Removes an installed application. Run by ENTER after the remove question.
1. Unless the answer was 'y', sets window 0 and redraws the Index.
2. Finds the installation handle whose DOR matches the application's (OS_Nq NQ_Ain, OS_Fn
FN_GH/FN_NH with HND_INST); RC_Fail when none does.
3. When the handle installed several applications, checks with OS_Poll and DC_Pol that none
of them runs (RC_Use otherwise).
4. Lowers the static handle of the processes of later applications by the number removed
(OS_Uash on each stacked process environment).
5. Unchains the DORs from the :APP.- front DOR ($4060 in bank $21), linking the son or the
preceding brother to the DOR after the removed group (GetSmallestBrother).
6. Closes the memory handle (OS_Mcl), frees the installation handle, polls the keys again
(InitKeys), writes "Removal completed." and waits for ESC; then MainLoop.
Error: stores the error code in ubIdxErrorCode, sets IDXF2_B_ERROR, sets window 0 and
redraws the Index. Does not return.

8856.synopsis:
Reads the brother pointer of a DOR: binds the DOR's bank into segment 1, reads its
DOR_BROTHER field and restores segment 1.
Entry: BHL = DOR.
Exit: BHL = brother DOR (0 when there is none).
Changes: AF, B, HL.
Keeps: C, DE, IY.

8890.synopsis:
Follows the brother chain from a DOR as many times as the installation handle has
applications (ihnd_AppNbOf), giving the DOR that comes after the installed group.
Entry: BHL = first DOR of the group; IX = installation handle.
Exit: BHL = DOR after the group.
Changes: AF, B, HL.
Keeps: C, DE, IY.

9056.synopsis:
Opens the remove window (GN_Win with RemoveWdBlock) and defines window 2 as its text area
(58 x 6 at column 13, row 2), selected and cleared.
Entry: none.

9080.synopsis:
GN_Win definition block of the remove window: window 2 with bars, shelf brackets and an
8-pixel banner on a greyed screen, at X = 9, Y = 0, 64 wide and 8 high; banner RemoveBanner.

9087.synopsis: Banner text of the remove window: "REMOVE APPLICATION", null-terminated.

9106.synopsis:
Index command <>NQ (entry in the command table): shows details of the selected entry. With
the application list active (window 0) it shows APPLICATION INFORMATION: name, type (good,
bad, ugly or popdown), device (ROM.n or APP.-), static handle, segment bindings, entry, and
the DOR, brother, topics, commands, help and tokens pointers. With the process list active
it shows PROCESS INFORMATION for the selected suspended process: PID, name, static and
process handles, flags, associated pointer and length, default device, match string and
directory (nothing for the Index itself or an empty list). Then "PRESS ESC TO RESUME",
active window 3 and a jump to MainLoop.
Entry: none. Does not return (IX is kept).

9913.synopsis:
Entry inside nq_cde: writes DE as 4 hex digits (D, then E) with OS_Hout.
Entry: DE = value.
Changes: AF.

9920.synopsis:
Reads a 3-byte pointer from an extended address with GN_Rbe: CDE = (BHL).
Entry: BHL = address of the pointer.
Exit: CDE = pointer; HL = address of its last byte.
Changes: AF, C, D, E, HL.

9935.synopsis:
Opens the <>NQ window with the given banner (GN_Win with InfoWdBlock), then selects and
clears window 2 and toggles tiny font.
Entry: DE = banner text.

9953.synopsis:
Moves the cursor to column 30 of the window (1,"2X"), the second column of the <>NQ display.
Entry: none.

9985.synopsis: Banner text of the process information window: "PROCESS INFORMATION", null-terminated.

10005.synopsis: The text "good", null-terminated: an application type name for <>NQ.

10010.synopsis: The text "bad", null-terminated: an application type name for <>NQ (AT_Bad set).

10014.synopsis: The text "ugly", null-terminated: an application type name for <>NQ (AT_Ugly set).

10019.synopsis: The text "popdown", null-terminated: an application type name for <>NQ (AT_Popd set).

10241.synopsis:
Releases what the OZ update holds: closes the config file (CloseCfgFile) and, when
App_MemHnd is not 0, closes the memory handle (ci_CloseMem); then App_MemHnd = 0.
Entry: none.
Exit: IX = 0.

10303.synopsis:
Closes the OZ update's config file when uwIdxCfgHnd holds a handle (GN_Cl) and stores the
returned IX (0) back.
Entry: uwIdxCfgHnd = file handle or 0.
Exit: IX = 0 when a file was closed; otherwise IX = 0 from uwIdxCfgHnd.
Changes: AF, IX.

11303.synopsis:
Converts an ASCII hex digit ('0'-'9', 'A'-'F'; upper case only) to its value.
Entry: A = character.
Exit: Fc = 0, A = 0-15.
Error: Fc = 1, A unchanged, when A is not a hex digit.
Changes: AF.

11444.synopsis:
Opens the OPERATING SYSTEM UPDATE window (GN_Win with UpdateWdBlock) and defines window 2 as
its text area (58 x 6 at column 13, row 2), selected and cleared.
Entry: none.

11468.synopsis:
Wildcard name of the OZ update config file searched in RAM: ":RAM.?/ozs?-*.upd",
null-terminated (the source's comments call it ozupdate.cfg).

11486.synopsis: Progress text "CRC Checking ", null-terminated, written before a bank file's name.

11500.synopsis: Progress text " bank file", CR, LF, null-terminated, written after a bank file's name.

11513.synopsis: Error text "CRC check failed for ", null-terminated, followed by the bank file's name.

11535.synopsis: Error text "Syntax error at line ", null-terminated, followed by the config line number.

11557.synopsis: Error text " in 'ozupdate.cfg' file.", CR, LF, null-terminated, after the line number.

11584.synopsis:
GN_Win definition block of the OZ update window: window 2 with bars, shelf brackets and an
8-pixel banner on a greyed screen, at X = 9, Y = 0, 64 wide and 8 high; banner UpdateBanner.

11591.synopsis: Banner text of the OZ update window: "OPERATING SYSTEM UPDATE", null-terminated.

11615.synopsis:
Separator table of the config file parser: a length byte (27) followed by the separator
characters (start_separators). The position of a character found by StrChr is its symbol
number (sym_null, sym_dquote, ...).

11616.synopsis:
The 27 separator characters of the config file parser: null, double quote, single quote, ; ,
. ( { } ) + - * / % ^ = & ~ | : ! < > #, CR and LF, in symbol order.

11643.synopsis: End of the separator table, used only to compute its length; the $FF filler follows.

261.synopsis:
Entry inside FPMod (FP_MOD), reached directly when both numbers are integers and called by
FPIdv: divides the 32-bit integer HLhl by the 32-bit integer DEde. Both are made positive,
Division runs the long division, and the remainder takes the sign of the dividend. There is
no check for a zero divisor.
Entry: HLhl = dividend; DEde = divisor (two's complement integers; C and B are not read).
Exit: HLhl = remainder (sign of the dividend), C = 0; DEde = quotient's magnitude; A bit 7 =
1 when the signs of the numbers differ.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, bc', de', hl', AF'.

340.synopsis:
Entry inside FPSub: flips the sign bit of DEdeB and goes on at add_2, so HLhlC = HLhlC -
DEdeB for two floats. Called by sub_0_E35F.
Entry: HLhlC, DEdeB = floats.
Exit: as add_2 (HLhlC = difference).
Error: A = RC_Tbg on exponent overflow, through FPError, which unwinds to the FP call's
frame (IY) and returns from the call.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, bc', de', hl', AF'.

346.synopsis:
Flips the sign bit of HLhlC and goes on at add_2, so HLhlC = DEdeB - HLhlC for two floats.
Used by the sine core to fold an argument (pi/4 - x), by FPAsn for 1 - x^2 and by the ATN
and ACS tails for pi/2 - x.
Entry: HLhlC, DEdeB = floats.
Exit: as add_2 (HLhlC = DEdeB - HLhlC).
Error: A = RC_Tbg on exponent overflow, through FPError, which unwinds to the FP call's
frame (IY) and returns from the call.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, bc', de', hl', AF'.

366.synopsis:
Entry inside FPAdd: adds two floats, HLhlC = HLhlC + DEdeB. A float has C = exponent + $80
(value = 1.m * 2^(C - $80)), H bit 7 = sign and the mantissa's top 1 implied; C = 0 is zero.
1. When DEdeB is zero HLhlC is returned; when HLhlC is zero DEdeB is returned (swapped in).
2. The number with the smaller exponent is moved into HLhlC and shifted right by Fix until
the exponents match; the bits shifted out go into bc'.
3. Equal signs add the mantissas (a carry shifts back one place and raises the exponent);
different signs subtract them, negating on a borrow, and NormalizeHLhlC realigns the result.
4. The result is rounded from bc' (IncHLhl, HalfIncHLhl), gets its sign back in H bit 7, and
a zero result becomes FPZer.
Entry: HLhlC, DEdeB = floats.
Exit: HLhlC = sum (float, or 0).
Error: A = RC_Tbg when the exponent overflows, through FPError, which unwinds to the FP
call's frame (IY) and returns from the call.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, bc', de', hl', AF'.

454.synopsis:
Entry inside FPDiv: divides two floats, HLhlC = HLhlC / DEdeB. The sign is the XOR of the
signs; the mantissas, with their top bits put back, go through Division (a 32-bit long
division), plus one more quotient bit (loc_0_E3FB) when the top bit is clear, and the
quotient is rounded. The exponent is C - B + $80, adjusted for normalisation. A zero
dividend returns zero; an underflow returns zero.
Entry: HLhlC = dividend, DEdeB = divisor (floats).
Exit: HLhlC = quotient.
Error: A = RC_Dvz when DEdeB is zero (B = 0), A = RC_Tbg when the exponent overflows,
through FPError, which unwinds to the FP call's frame (IY) and returns from the call.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, bc', de', hl', AF'.

601.synopsis:
FP_MUL: multiplies HLhlC by DEdeB. When both are integers (B = C = 0) the magnitudes are
multiplied into a 64-bit product by div_2 (the integer multiply, despite its name), which
returns an integer when the product fits in 31 bits and a float otherwise; any float operand
turns both into floats (FltBoth) and mul_1 multiplies them. Also called by FPPwr for
repeated squaring. The callers listed in apps/calculator/calc.asm call the calculator's own
FpMul, not this routine.
Entry: HLhlC, DEdeB = numbers (exponent 0: 32-bit integer in HLhl; otherwise a float).
Exit: Fc = 0; HLhlC = product.
Error: Fc = 1, A = RC_Tbg when a float product overflows.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, bc', de', hl', AF'.

609.synopsis:
Entry inside FPMul: multiplies two floats, HLhlC = HLhlC * DEdeB. The sign is the XOR of the
signs; the mantissas, with their top bits put back, are multiplied by sub_0_E40E (plus a
last shift by sub_0_E422 on a carry), the 64-bit product is rounded to 32 bits and the
exponents are added (mul_2). The FPP's main multiply, used by the series and power routines.
Entry: HLhlC, DEdeB = floats.
Exit: HLhlC = product; zero when either is zero or the exponent underflows.
Error: A = RC_Tbg when the exponent overflows, through FPError, which unwinds to the FP
call's frame (IY) and returns from the call.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, bc', de', hl', AF'.

1135.synopsis:
Entry inside FPSqr for a float: square root of HLhlC. The exponent is halved (the mantissa
shifted one place first when the exponent is even), sub_0_E441 produces the root's bits by
the restoring method, two more steps (sub_0_E441, sub_0_E47A, loc_0_E3FB) give the rounding
bit, and the root is rounded. Also called by FPAsn.
Entry: HLhlC = float.
Exit: HLhlC = square root (zero for zero); A = 0.
Error: A = RC_Nvr when HLhlC is negative, through FPError, which unwinds to the FP call's
frame (IY) and returns from the call.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, bc', de', hl'.

1247.synopsis:
Entry inside FPCos for a float: cosine of HLhlC (radians). sub_0_E1DA reduces |x| modulo
pi/4 and returns the count of eighth turns in E; adding 2 (a quarter turn) makes it a sine,
which the shared core loc_0_DCF5 evaluates. Also called by FPTan.
Entry: HLhlC = float (radians).
Exit: HLhlC = cos x.
Error: A = RC_Acl when |x| >= 2^23, through FPError, which unwinds to the FP call's frame
(IY) and returns from the call.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, bc', de', hl', AF', IX.

1258.synopsis:
Entry inside FPSin for a float: sine of HLhlC (radians). sub_0_E1DA reduces |x| modulo pi/4
(count of eighth turns in E); the sign of x goes into bit 2 of that count and the code falls
into sub_0_DCF1, the core shared with cos_1: an odd eighth is folded (pi/4 - r), eighths 0
and 3 use the sine series in r^2 times r, 1 and 2 the cosine series, and bit 2 gives the
sign. Also called by FPTan.
Entry: HLhlC = float (radians).
Exit: HLhlC = sin x.
Error: A = RC_Acl when |x| >= 2^23, through FPError, which unwinds to the FP call's frame
(IY) and returns from the call.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, bc', de', hl', AF', IX.

1387.synopsis:
Loads the float 1.0 into DEdeB (DEde = 0, B = $80).
Entry: none.
Exit: DEdeB = 1.0.
Changes: B, DE, de'.
Keeps: AF, C, HL, bc', hl'.

1528.synopsis:
Reciprocal: HLhlC = 1 / HLhlC. Loads 1.0 into DEdeB (LdDEdeB_1) and falls into loc_0_DDFB,
which swaps the two and divides. Used by FPPwr for a negative power, by FPExp and by FPAtn
(arguments above tan(3*pi/8)).
Entry: HLhlC = float.
Exit: HLhlC = 1 / x.
Error: A = RC_Dvz when HLhlC is zero, through FPError, which unwinds to the FP call's frame
(IY) and returns from the call.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, bc', de', hl', AF'.

1531.synopsis:
Entry inside sub_0_DDF8: swaps HLhlC and DEdeB and jumps to div_1, so HLhlC = DEdeB / HLhlC.
Called by FPAsn to form x / sqrt(1 - x^2).
Entry: HLhlC = divisor, DEdeB = dividend (floats).
Exit: HLhlC = DEdeB / HLhlC.
Error: A = RC_Dvz when HLhlC is zero, through FPError, which unwinds to the FP call's frame
(IY) and returns from the call.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, bc', de', hl', AF'.

1537.synopsis:
Loads ln 2 into DEdeB ($3172:$17F8, exponent $7F: 0.6931472). FPExp then adjusts de' and
loads bc' = $D1CF for 48 bits of ln 2; sub_0_DE0F multiplies the power of two by it.
Entry: none.
Exit: DEdeB = ln 2.
Changes: B, DE, de'.
Keeps: AF, C, HL, bc', hl'.

1551.synopsis:
Entry inside FPLn for a float: natural logarithm of HLhlC. Also called by FPPwr (x^y as
exp(y ln x)) and through FPLn by FPLog.
1. Splits x into m * 2^n with m from sqrt(1/2) to sqrt(2): the exponent is set to $80, and
to $7F when the mantissa reaches sqrt(2) ($3504F333).
2. t = (m - 1) / (m + 1) (sub_0_E35F); ln m = t * P(t^2), the series evaluated by sub_0_E37D
from the five coefficients after the call.
3. Adds n * ln 2 (n made a float from the exponent byte, sub_0_DE01) with add_2.
Entry: HLhlC = float.
Exit: HLhlC = ln x; A = 0.
Error: A = RC_Lgr when x is zero or negative, through FPError, which unwinds to the FP
call's frame (IY) and returns from the call.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, bc', de', hl', AF', IX.

1694.synopsis:
FP_ASN: arc sine of HLhlC, in radians. Computes 1 - x^2 (mul_1, sub_3) and its square root
(sqr_1); when that is zero (|x| = 1) the result is pi/2 with the sign of x, otherwise x /
sqrt(1 - x^2) goes to the arc tangent code (loc_0_DEC6 in FPAtn). Also called by FPAcs,
which returns pi/2 minus the result.
Entry: HLhlC = number (an integer is made a float).
Exit: Fc = 0; HLhlC = arc sine (float).
Error: Fc = 1, A = RC_Nvr when |x| > 1.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, bc', de', hl', AF', IX.

2247.synopsis:
Loads DEdeB from a 5-byte float at IX in memory order: (IX+0) = e, (IX+1) = d, (IX+2) = E,
(IX+3) = D, (IX+4) = exponent into B. Reads the coefficient tables of sub_0_E37D and the
number FPPwr keeps on the stack.
Entry: IX = 5-byte number.
Exit: DEdeB = number.
Changes: B, DE, de'.
Keeps: AF, C, HL, IX, bc', hl'.

2270.synopsis:
The number reader of FPVal (FP_VAL): reads unsigned decimal digits at IX into HLhlC. Integer
digits accumulate in HLhl (sub_0_E16B); once HLhl would overflow, later digits only raise a
decimal exponent (C). An optional '.' starts the fraction digits, counted in B (sub_0_E169),
and an 'E' or 'e' the exponent (sub_0_E13A). Without point and exponent, a value below 2^31
is returned as an integer; otherwise HLhl is normalised to a float and multiplied or divided
by the power of ten from sub_0_E3A4 (in steps of 10^38 for very small numbers).
Entry: IX = first character after the sign; IY = FP call frame (for ReadByteIX).
Exit: HLhlC = unsigned value (integer or float); IX = first character after the number.
Error: A = RC_Bdn for a second decimal point, A = RC_Tbg when the value overflows, through
FPError, which unwinds to the FP call's frame (IY) and returns from the call.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, bc', de', hl', AF', IX.

2362.synopsis:
Reads the exponent after the 'E' of a number for sub_0_E0DE: skips the 'E', blanks and a '+'
or '-' (GetNumStart), then reads decimal digits into a byte. Two digits give 0 to 99; a
third digit or more gives 100. A '-' negates the result.
Entry: IX = the 'E'; A = 0; IY = FP call frame (for ReadByteIX).
Exit: A = exponent (signed byte); IX = first character after the digits.
Changes: AF, DE, IX, AF'.
Keeps: BC, HL.

2464.synopsis:
Converts both numbers to integers: FPFix on DEdeB (swapped in and out by ExHLhlC_DEdeB) and
then falls into FPFix for HLhlC. Used by the integer operations (AND, OR, EOR, MOD, DIV)
when either operand is a float.
Entry: HLhlC, DEdeB = numbers.
Exit: HLhl, DEde = 32-bit integers, C = B = 0.
Error: A = RC_Tbg when a float is 2^31 or more in size, through FPError, which unwinds to
the FP call's frame (IY) and returns from the call.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, bc', de', hl', AF'.

2473.synopsis:
FP_FIX: truncates HLhlC to an integer (towards zero). An integer (C = 0) is returned as it
is. A float has its top bit put back, is shifted right by Fix until the exponent reaches
$9F, and is negated when it was negative. Also called by FPNot and FixBoth.
Entry: HLhlC = number (C = 0: 32-bit two's complement integer in HLhl; otherwise a float, C
= exponent + $80, H bit 7 = sign).
Exit: Fc = 0; HLhl = integer, C = 0.
Error: Fc = 1, A = RC_Tbg when |x| >= 2^31.
Changes: AF, C, HL, bc', hl', AF'.

2488.synopsis:
Negates the 32-bit integer HLhl (two's complement: HLhl = 0 - HLhl). The tail of FPFix for a
negative number.
Entry: HLhl = integer.
Exit: HLhl = -HLhl.
Changes: F, HL, hl'.
Keeps: A, BC, DE, bc', de'.

2508.synopsis:
Negates the 48-bit mantissa HLhl:bc' (bc' holds the extra low bits) and complements A, which
holds the sign in add_2. Used by add_2 when subtracting the mantissas borrowed.
Entry: HLhl:bc' = mantissa; A = sign byte.
Exit: HLhl:bc' = 0 - HLhl:bc'; A = NOT A.
Changes: AF, HL, bc', hl'.
Keeps: DE, de'.

2522.synopsis:
Argument reduction for SIN and COS: loads DEdeB = pi/4 (loc_0_DD76) with 16 further bits of
it in bc' ($2169), and falls into sub_0_E1EA, which reduces |x| modulo pi/4.
Entry: HLhlC = float.
Exit: HLhlC = remainder, normalised with H bit 7 set (the callers clear it); E = eighth
turns in x (bit 7 set from 128 on).
Error: A = RC_Acl when |x| >= 2^23 (exponent above $96), through FPError, which unwinds to
the FP call's frame (IY) and returns from the call.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, bc', de', hl', IX.

2538.synopsis:
Reduces |HLhlC| modulo |DEdeB|, the divisor's mantissa extended by 16 more bits in bc': a
restoring long division on the 48-bit mantissas, one quotient bit per exponent step, the low
bits of the quotient collected in C. The remainder is normalised by NormalizeHLhlC. Called
by FPExp with ln 2 and by sub_0_E1DA with pi/4.
Entry: HLhlC = dividend, DEdeB = divisor (floats, signs ignored); bc' = 16 more bits of the
divisor.
Exit: HLhlC = remainder, normalised with H bit 7 set; E = quotient's low 7 bits, bit 7 set
once the quotient reached 128; D bit 7 set; IX = 0.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, bc', hl', IX.

2617.synopsis:
Normalises a mantissa that carries extra bits: while H bit 7 is clear, shifts HLhl:bc' left
one place and decrements the exponent C. Stops with C = 0 when it runs out (zero or
underflow).
Entry: HLhl:bc' = mantissa; C = exponent.
Exit: H bit 7 set and C reduced, or C = 0.
Changes: F, C, HL, bc', hl'.

2635.synopsis:
Normalises HLhl with zeros shifted in: while H bit 7 is clear, shifts HLhl left one place
and decrements C. Stops with C = 0 when it runs out. FPFlt, sub_0_E0DE and sub_0_DE0F make
floats from integers with it.
Entry: HLhl = mantissa; C = exponent.
Exit: H bit 7 set and C reduced, or C = 0.
Changes: F, C, HL, hl'.

2648.synopsis:
Converts both numbers to floats: FPFlt on DEdeB (swapped in and out by ExHLhlC_DEdeB) and
then falls into FPFlt for HLhlC. Called by every two-operand function when either operand is
a float.
Entry: HLhlC, DEdeB = numbers.
Exit: HLhlC, DEdeB = floats (an integer zero stays zero).
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, de', hl'.

2657.synopsis:
FP_FLT: converts an integer in HLhlC to a float. A float (C <> 0) and zero are returned as
they are. Otherwise the magnitude is normalised from exponent $9F (Normalize0HLhlC) and H
bit 7, the implied top bit, is replaced by the sign. A float's value is 1.m * 2^(C - $80).
Entry: HLhlC = number (C = 0: 32-bit two's complement integer in HLhl).
Exit: Fc = 0; HLhlC = float (C = exponent + $80, H bit 7 = sign).
Changes: AF, C, HL, hl'.
Keeps: B, DE, bc', de'.

2679.synopsis:
Adds 1 to the 32-bit HLhl. Used by the rounding steps and by FPInt and FPSgn.
Entry: HLhl = value.
Exit: HLhl = HLhl + 1; Fc = 1 when it wrapped from $FFFFFFFF to 0; bc' = 1.
Changes: F, HL, bc', hl'.
Keeps: A, BC, DE, de'.

2699.synopsis:
Swaps the numbers HLhlC and DEdeB: exchanges C and B and falls into ExHLhl_DEde.
Entry: HLhlC, DEdeB = numbers.
Exit: the two swapped; A = old C.
Changes: A, BC, DE, HL, de', hl'.
Keeps: F.

2702.synopsis:
Swaps the 32-bit HLhl and DEde in both register sets. Used by sub_0_E16B to put back the
value saved before an overflowing multiply by 10.
Entry: HLhl, DEde = values.
Exit: the two swapped.
Changes: DE, HL, de', hl'.
Keeps: AF, BC, bc'.

2707.synopsis:
Shifts the mantissa HLhl right one place into the extra bits bc' (the bit leaving c' is
lost) and ORs b' into A', so that A' turns non-zero once a 1 bit has left HLhl (Fix clears
A' first). Then falls into IncC to raise the exponent.
Entry: HLhl:bc' = mantissa; C = exponent.
Exit: HLhl:bc' halved; C = C + 1.
Error: A = RC_Tbg when C wraps to 0, through FPError, which unwinds to the FP call's frame
(IY) and returns from the call.
Changes: F, C, HL, bc', hl', AF'.

2719.synopsis:
Increments the exponent C; when it wraps to 0 it falls into ErrTooBig.
Entry: C = exponent.
Exit: C = C + 1.
Error: A = RC_Tbg when C wraps to 0, through FPError, which unwinds to the FP call's frame
(IY) and returns from the call.
Changes: F, C.

2737.synopsis:
Tests the 32-bit HLhl for zero: A = H OR L OR h OR l.
Entry: HLhl = value.
Exit: Fz = 1 when HLhl is zero; A = the OR of its bytes.
Changes: AF.
Keeps: BC, DE, HL, bc', de', hl'.

2817.synopsis:
One decade step of FPStr's digit scaling: decrements the decimal exponent B, then multiplies
the unnormalised mantissa by 10: C goes up by 3 and HLhl becomes HLhl + HLhl/4 (falls into
sub_0_E303 and AddHLhl_DEde). The bit carried out of the mantissa comes back in Fc.
Entry: HLhl = mantissa (top bit set); C = exponent; B = decimal exponent.
Exit: B = B - 1; C = C + 3; HLhl = 1.25 * HLhl (low 32 bits); Fc = carry out; DEde = old
HLhl.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, de', hl', AF'.

2829.synopsis:
Adds the 32-bit DEde to HLhl.
Entry: HLhl, DEde = values.
Exit: HLhl = HLhl + DEde; Fc = carry out; P/V = signed overflow.
Changes: F, HL, hl'.
Keeps: A, BC, DE, bc', de'.

2835.synopsis:
Subtracts the 32-bit DEde from HLhl. FPSub and FPAdd try integer arithmetic with it and
AddHLhl_DEde first, and turn to floats when P/V shows a signed overflow.
Entry: HLhl, DEde = values.
Exit: HLhl = HLhl - DEde; Fc = borrow; P/V = signed overflow.
Changes: F, HL, hl'.
Keeps: A, BC, DE, bc', de'.

2843.synopsis:
Multiplies the 32-bit unsigned HLhl by 10 as ((HLhl * 4) + HLhl) * 2, keeping the original
in DEde, and falls into HLhl_x2 for the last doubling. Used by sub_0_E16B to collect decimal
digits.
Entry: HLhl = value.
Exit: HLhl = 10 * HLhl; DEde = old HLhl; Fc = 1 on overflow (HLhl then partly multiplied).
Changes: F, DE, HL, de', hl'.

2858.synopsis:
Doubles the 32-bit HLhl (shift left one place).
Entry: HLhl = value.
Exit: HLhl = 2 * HLhl; Fc = the bit shifted out.
Changes: F, HL, hl'.
Keeps: A, BC, DE, bc', de'.

2865.synopsis:
Shifts the 32-bit HLhl right one place (logical; H bit 7 becomes 0). SrlHLhlC0, the entry
before it, also increments C.
Entry: HLhl = value.
Exit: HLhl = HLhl / 2; Fc = the bit shifted out.
Changes: F, HL, hl'.
Keeps: A, BC, DE, bc', de'.

2876.synopsis:
Copies the number HLhlC into DEdeB: B = C and falls into LdDEde_HLhl.
Entry: HLhlC = number.
Exit: DEdeB = HLhlC.
Changes: B, DE, de'.
Keeps: AF, C, HL, bc', hl'.

2877.synopsis:
Copies the 32-bit HLhl into DEde.
Entry: HLhl = value.
Exit: DEde = HLhl.
Changes: DE, de'.
Keeps: AF, BC, HL, bc', hl'.

2884.synopsis:
Squares HLhlC (LdDEdeB_HLhlC, mul_1) and falls into PushHLhlC, which leaves the square on
the stack as well: the set-up of the series in SIN, COS, LN and ATN before sub_0_E37D.
Entry: HLhlC = float x.
Exit: HLhlC = x^2; x^2 pushed on the caller's stack (three words, as PushHLhlC).
Error: A = RC_Tbg when the square overflows, through FPError, which unwinds to the FP call's
frame (IY) and returns from the call.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, bc', de', hl', AF', IX.

2890.synopsis:
Pushes the number HLhlC on the caller's stack and returns: takes the return address into IX,
pushes BC, HL and hl' (hl' on top, six bytes) and jumps back through IX. PopDEdeB takes the
number back into DEdeB.
Entry: HLhlC = number.
Exit: HLhlC on the stack; SP = SP - 6 for the caller.
Changes: IX.
Keeps: AF, BC, DE, HL, bc', de', hl'.

2899.synopsis:
Pops a number pushed by PushHLhlC into DEdeB and returns: takes the return address into IX,
pops de', DE, then the pushed BC, whose C becomes B. C is kept.
Entry: a number from PushHLhlC on the stack.
Exit: DEdeB = that number; SP = SP + 6 for the caller; A = C.
Changes: A, B, DE, de', IX.
Keeps: F, C, HL, bc', hl'.

2911.synopsis:
Computes HLhlC = (x - 1) / (x + 1): x + 1 (add_2 with 1.0) is kept on the stack, x - 1 is
formed by sub_2, and div_1 divides. Used by FPLn on the mantissa and by FPAtn for arguments
between tan(pi/8) and tan(3*pi/8).
Entry: HLhlC = float x.
Exit: HLhlC = (x - 1) / (x + 1).
Error: A = RC_Dvz when x = -1, through FPError, which unwinds to the FP call's frame (IY)
and returns from the call.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, bc', de', hl', AF', IX.

2941.synopsis:
Evaluates a polynomial whose coefficients follow the CALL as 5-byte floats (mantissa low
byte first, exponent last), in Horner form: r = t * c0 + c1, r = r * t + c2, and so on.
Coefficients have exponents below $80; the first with an exponent of $80 or more (1.0 or
2.0) is the last one, and the routine returns onto it: its bytes run as four NOPs and an
ADD, so execution goes on after the table.
Entry: HLhlC = t; t also on the stack under the return address (PushHLhlC or sub_0_E344).
Exit: HLhlC = polynomial value; t still on the stack (the caller pops it with PopDEdeB).
Error: A = RC_Tbg on overflow, through FPError, which unwinds to the FP call's frame (IY)
and returns from the call.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, bc', de', hl', AF', IX.

2980.synopsis:
Builds a power of ten in DEdeB by repeated multiplication by 10 (sub_0_E303, rounded),
keeping HLhlC. With A from 0 to $7F, DEdeB = 10^A. With A of $80 or more, A is an exponent
byte: it stops at the first power of ten whose exponent byte is above A. FPStr scales by it;
sub_0_E0DE applies the decimal exponent with it.
Entry: A = power, or exponent limit; HLhlC = number to keep.
Exit: DEdeB = 10^k (positive float); A = k; HLhlC unchanged.
Error: A = RC_Tbg when the power overflows, through FPError, which unwinds to the FP call's
frame (IY) and returns from the call.
Changes: AF, B, DE, bc', de', AF'.
Keeps: C, HL, hl'.

3067.synopsis:
Entry inside Division, called with the alternate register set active: shifts the carry into
the remainder HLhl (doubling it), subtracts the divisor BCbc when it fits and shifts the
quotient bit into DEde, repeating until A counts up to a positive value. With A at 0 or
above it gives exactly one more quotient bit; div_1 and sqr_1 use it so.
Entry: HLhl = remainder; BCbc = divisor; DEde = quotient so far; A = step counter; Fc = bit
to shift in.
Exit: DEde = quotient with the new bits; HLhl = remainder; A incremented.
Changes: AF, DE, HL, de', hl'.

3086.synopsis:
Unsigned shift-and-add multiply, called with the alternate register set active (the callers
load the numbers and EXX): for each step the 64-bit HLhl:DEde moves right one place and BCbc
is added to HLhl when the bit leaving DEde is 1. Used by mul_1 (32 steps) and the integer
multiply div_2 (33 steps).
Entry: HLhl = 0; DEde = multiplier; BCbc = multiplicand; A = minus the number of steps.
Exit: HLhl:DEde = product; A = 0; Fc = carry from the last addition (mul_1 then shifts once
more with sub_0_E422).
Changes: AF, DE, HL, de', hl'.

3137.synopsis:
The square-root loop of sqr_1, called with the alternate register set active: each step
shifts two bits of the radicand DEde into the remainder HLhl, tries to subtract the trial
root formed in BCbc and keeps or restores, adding one bit to the root. Repeats until A
counts up to a positive value.
Entry: HLhl = remainder; DEde = radicand bits to come; BCbc = root so far; A = minus the
number of steps.
Exit: BCbc = root; HLhl = remainder; A = 0 when the steps ran out.
Changes: AF, BC, DE, HL, bc', de', hl'.

3194.synopsis:
The last square-root step of sqr_1, with no radicand bits left: doubles the remainder HLhl,
increments C and subtracts the trial root BCbc when it fits (undoing it otherwise). When the
doubling overflows it subtracts without the test and goes on at the loop's end (loc_0_E46F).
Entry: HLhl = remainder; BCbc = root; A = step counter (alternate register set active).
Exit: HLhl = new remainder; C incremented when the subtraction stood; A incremented.
Changes: AF, C, HL, hl'.

3245.synopsis:
Reads the byte at IX for FPVal's number reader. An address in segment 3 ($C000-$FFFF), where
the FPP itself runs, is read through segment 1: the caller's S3 bank (from the call frame,
IY+OSFrame_S3) is bound into segment 1 for the read and BLSC_SR1 is restored after it.
Entry: IX = address; IY = FP call frame.
Exit: A = byte; DE = IX.
Changes: A, DE, A' (segment 3 only: it then holds the old BLSC_SR1).
Keeps: F, BC, HL, IX.

3286.synopsis:
Writes A to the byte at HL for FPStr. An address in segment 3 ($C000-$FFFF), where the FPP
itself runs, is written through segment 1: the caller's S3 bank (from the call frame,
IY+OSFrame_S3) is bound into segment 1 for the write and BLSC_SR1 is restored after it.
Entry: A = byte; HL = address; IY = FP call frame.
Exit: byte written.
Changes: A' (segment 3 only: it then holds the old BLSC_SR1).
Keeps: AF, BC, DE, HL.

labels.name: FileArea
labels.synopsis:
The ROM's FlashStore file area, the preset 'oz' file area below the OZ banks. It holds one
file entry: the name's length, the name, the file's length (4 bytes, low byte first) and its
bytes. The rest of the bank is $FF, free space for more entries.

labels.name: WelcomeData
labels.synopsis:
The file, a PipeDream document: the OZ 4.7 release notes (filearea/welcome.pdd in the
OZ source).

labels.name: FileAreaFree
labels.synopsis: Free space to the end of the bank: every byte $FF.
